title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards outlines its commitment to improving transparency, accountability and safety in AI systems. It highlights key policy actions, including the development of new guidelines and regulatory measures, to ensure AI technologies are aligned with public interests and ethical standards.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: The European Commission’s Regulation 2024/1689 sets out uniform rules for artificial intelligence across the EU, focusing on safety, transparency, and accountability. It updates and amends existing AI‑related regulations and directives to create a more coherent, harmonised legal framework for developers, users, and regulators.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual outlines its plan to oversee and control the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to keep exams fair, reliable, and secure. The document details how the regulator will work with government ministers and education partners to set clear rules, monitor compliance, and protect the integrity of assessments.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used to train AI systems, assessing the legal, economic, and societal effects on creators, users, and the AI industry. It offers recommendations and best practices to balance copyright protection with the need for data and innovation.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government replies to the Lords Select Committee report by recognizing the urgent need for better AI governance and outlining concrete steps to improve oversight, research, and workforce readiness. It pledges to strengthen regulatory frameworks, boost public investment in AI, and promote transparency and accountability across the sector.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document sets out the purpose, scope, and duties of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence affects public standards and guidelines. It also includes a list of frequently asked questions to help people understand the review process and what the committee will do.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence, outlining its views on regulatory frameworks and responsible AI development. The submission aims to inform policymakers about best practices and potential risks associated with AI deployment.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explains how artificial intelligence will change the rules for medical products, aiming to keep them safe and effective while encouraging innovation. It applies the key principles from the AI White Paper—such as transparency, accountability, and risk management—to guide the design, approval, and ongoing monitoring of AI‑enabled medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy sets out a goal for the organisation to become the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence entity in AI relative to its size. It focuses on adopting advanced AI capabilities to boost operational effectiveness, streamline processes, and strengthen security while maintaining public trust.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to take advantage of AI’s potential. It also outlines measures to manage and mitigate the risks that come with using AI in transportation.
